title: Opportunistic backfill scraps and decision log — 2026-06-27
content:
Context:
This is a working notes + decision log from the ops huddle focused on opportunistic backfill heuristics (how we consume idle/slack GPU capacity in each region) and the short-term rules we can apply without changing core allocator code. Goal is to capture experiments, quick wins, and ownerable next steps so the next on-call can pick up where we left off.

Attendees:
- Evelyn Chen (owner)
- Marco Gomez
- Priya Nair
- Liam O'Connor
- Jinwoo Park
- (notes: many on mobile, fast-paced)

High-level summary (one-liner):
We validated a conservative backfill policy that uses a 15-minute soft lease for opportunistic jobs in us-west1 and eu-west3, implemented a skiplist for fragile models, and agreed on a short rollout to capture spare capacity while protecting high-priority dedicated workloads.

Observations from telemetry this week:
- Us-west1: observed ~320 surplus GPU-minutes/hour during off-peak (0100-0500 PDT) that are currently not utilized; spike windows are irregular but predictable by weekday.
- Eu-west3: surplus is smaller (~60 GPU-minutes/hour) but has higher churn due to preemptions; H100 pool shows 12% lower utilization vs. A100 pool for small-chat workloads.
- Preemption rate for opportunistic tasks currently: 2.1% in the last 7 days (mostly at region rebalance times).
- Customer model sensitivity: 4/24 top customers flagged model artifact locking issues when VFS mounted volumes are reclaimed mid-run (ticketed).

Immediate decisions (what we agreed to):
1) Soft-lease window: opportunistic backfill jobs get a 15-minute soft lease before we force-drain; this balances throughput with reduced tail preemption cost. (Owner: Evelyn)
2) Skiplist for fragile models: ops will maintain a skiplist of models (by model-id) that are not allowed into opportunistic backfill due to known stateful artifacts. Initial list: [model-legacy-v2, img2text-attach-1]. (Owner: Marco)
3) Region affinity rule: prefer backfill in-region with no cross-region migration for opportunistic jobs to avoid egress and reduce failure surface. (Owner: Priya)
4) Cost-signal cap: opportunistic jobs may be limited to X tokens/sec equivalent per GPU to avoid noisy neighbors for dedicated pools — implement as a soft throttle at the allocator level. (Owner: Jinwoo)

Heuristic sketch (for allocator/config only, not rollout code changes):
- Eligibility filter: model not in skiplist AND job duration expectation <= 25m AND memory footprint <= 70% of node.
- Scoring: score = (idle_time_score * 0.5) + (cost_savings_score * 0.2) + (preemption_risk_score * -0.3) + (priority_band_score * -0.1).
- Tie-breaker: prefer shorter wall-time predictions to minimize wasted preemption work.
- Backoff: if a region experiences > 5 preemptions in 1h, temporarily disable opportunistic scheduling for 30 minutes.

Experiment plan (A/B for 48h in us-west1):
A: Baseline (no change) for current opportunistic flow.
B: Apply soft-lease + skiplist + in-region affinity + 15% throttle on tokens/sec.
Metrics to capture:
- Opportunistic throughput (GPU-minutes consumed)
- Preemption rate (jobs/hour)
- Customer impact signals (error-rate for dedicated routes, latency p95)
- Cost delta (estimated token-cost saved)

Runbook snippets (quick ops play actions):
- If customer errors spike after rollout, immediately flip backfill flag via /admin/allocator/flags/backfill-enable (feature-flag).
- To add item to skiplist: create PR in infra-config repo (path: infra-config/backfill/skiplist.txt) and tag @marco for review.
- Emergency drain: /admin/allocator/drain-region <region> will evict opportunistic jobs first.

Open risks and unknowns:
- Statefulness: some internal inference jobs use ephemeral local state (VFS mounts) and are not safe to preempt. Current detection heuristics are brittle — need deeper integration with job descriptors.
- Billing reconciliation for opportunistic work when dedicated customers are billed by GPU-hours — need finance confirmation on attribution if opportunistic consumes previously reserved time. (Raised INFRA-3499)
- Edge nodes (small-gpu nodes) have higher variance; throttle may be insufficient to avoid contention.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Evelyn: push 48h A/B experiment config to staging and schedule rollout to us-west1 — ETA 2026-06-30.
- Marco: curate initial skiplist and open infra-config PR; also add detection note for VFS-mounted runs — ETA 2026-06-28.
- Priya: work with telemetry to add a new dashboard (opportunistic: idle vs consumed, preemptions) and add alert trigger at preemption>5/h — ETA 2026-06-29.
- Jinwoo: prototype tokens/sec soft throttle as allocator config knob and add unit tests — ETA 2026-07-02.
- Liam: draft customer-facing note for CS to explain opportunistic backfill (risk profile) in case users ask — ETA 2026-07-01.

Notes-to-self / rough ideas for follow-ups (brainstorm):
- Consider using short-lived checkpointing for opportunistic jobs that can save progress before preemption (local state snapshots to object store).
- Evaluate a paused-resume primitive in the runtime to reduce wasted compute on preempted runs.
- Investigate tagging certain GPU SKUs with "low-latency backfill" label to create predictable pockets for small experiments.

Meeting wrap + next check-in:
- Follow-up huddle Friday 09:30 PDT to review initial telemetry after the staged rollout (Evelyn will lead).
- If telemetry shows >10% increase in dedicated p95 latency, rollback immediately and trigger postmortem.

Appendix (quick data dump):
- Snapshot: us-west1 spare capacity 2026-06-25 02:00-04:00 PDT = 320 GPU-minutes/hr (median)
- Example failing model: model-legacy-v2 (observed mid-run mount error when preempted)
- Relevant tickets: INFRA-3421 (backfill policy request), INFRA-3499 (billing attribution question)

End of note. This doc is intentionally informal — we will polish into a playbook doc if the experiment succeeds.
